items.title: CVE-2026-130901 - Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server
items.summary:
Bulletin ID:  2026-195-AWS   Publication Date:  11/20/2026 10:30 AM PST  
  Description:   
 Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the file access checks in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server 1.0.10 through 1.0.20 might allow a context-dependent actor, via crafted document content processed by an MCP client, to read files outside the intended base directory and, in 1.0.12 through 1.0.20, to write PNG slide images outside it. This occurs when DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR is not set or is empty and the CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST environment variable is present. Versions before 1.0.10 do not restrict file access to a base directory.  
  Impacted versions:  >= 1.0.10 AND < 1.0.21  
   Refer to the article  for the most up-to-date and complete information.

items.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary:
CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its   Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog  , based on evidence of active exploitation. 
 
   CVE-2025-42884   SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability 
   CVE-2026-76466   Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability 
   CVE-2026-123890   VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability 
   CVE-2026-129448   Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability 
 
 These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.  
   Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk   establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.  
 
 
 While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of   KEV Catalog vulnerabilities  . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the   specified criteria  .  
 
 
 Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s   KEV Nomination Form  . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries
items.summary: This release we have three pull requests from  jburgess-r7  building out coverage for the identity-boundary issues detailed in Rapid7's  Breaking Zimbra Identity Boundaries, Part One  research.  First up is a new shared mixin,  Msf::Exploit::Remote::HTTP::Zimbra , which gives every current and future Zimbra module a common foundation for account/admin SOAP authentication, canonical identity resolution, mailbox-server lookup, and version parsing, allowing future modules to stay focused on the vulnerability instead of re-implementing Zimbra's SOAP plumbing.  Built on top of that mixin are two new modules targeting CVEs from the same research track:   CVE-2026-73571  ( #22080 ) It's an authorization bypass in Zimbra's SaveDraftRequest handling that lets an ordinary authenticated user send mail as another local mailbox without a delegation grant, landing a message in the victim's own Sent folder in the process.   CVE-2026-93637  ( #22070 ) Is a rate-limit bypass in Zimbra's Network Edition GraphQL authentication endpoint, which lets credential-stuffing attempts skip the source-IP lockout counter that normally protects the SOAP login path.  Both modules were validated against live Zimbra 10.1.16 Network Edition instances. Super cool contributions from our very own  jburgess-r7 .
